items.title: Fighters too small with empty mat dominating the frame
items.what: In every in-bout shot (e.g. the neutral stance frames and the Front Kick / Lunge Punch frames) the two fighters occupy roughly the middle horizontal band while a large empty tatami stretch sits under their feet and a tall dojo void sits above their heads. On a 390×844 portrait canvas they read as small action figures, not duelists.
items.why: First-second readability and impact collapse. On a phone held at arm’s length the sprites and their hit sparks become hard to parse; the cinematic ‘karate movie’ fantasy the art direction wants never lands because the camera is too wide.
items.how: Lower the camera, push it closer, and frame so the fighters’ heads sit near the upper third and their feet near the lower third (roughly 55–65 % of canvas height). Keep the same dojo backdrop; just crop tighter. Re-tune the existing vignette so it still softens the edges after the tighter crop.

items.title: Twin sticks sit too low and leave a dead zone under the fighters
items.what: Across the fight UI screens the two large circular stick bases sit at the very bottom edge of the 844-px-tall portrait frame, with a wide empty dark band between the bottom of the tatami and the top of the sticks. Thumbs must travel to the bezel.
items.why: On a real phone the lower bezel and the user’s grip already steal reach. Placing both sticks at the extreme bottom forces constant thumb travel, slows stance/technique changes, and makes the lower third of the 3D scene feel wasted.
items.how: Raise both stick clusters 64–96 px so their tops sit closer to the fighters’ feet. Slightly reduce stick diameter if needed to preserve the safe area, and keep the existing ‘Left-handed layout’ swap. Re-test with thumb zones on a physical 390-wide device.

items.title: IPON / win call is readable but the following result screen is sparse
items.what: The ‘IPON HASANABI SPINNING BACK KICK’ moment is clear, yet the subsequent full-result screen (‘HASANABI WINS 0—2½’) shows only a large title, a thin score line, a tiny ‘BOUTS WON 0/1’ pill, and a single REMATCH button over a dimmed action freeze. No next-round cue, no reward beat, no clear loser feedback beyond the score.
items.why: After the excitement of the ippon the player is dropped into a quiet, under-specified screen. On a mobile session this is exactly when retention or ‘one more round’ intent is decided; the sparse layout lets energy leak away.
items.how: Add a short vertical stack under the score: round outcome chip, a one-line coach note (‘Patience punished the wind-up’), and dual CTAs—REMATCH (primary) and NEXT QUALIFIER (secondary). Keep the warm tungsten palette and the frozen kick pose as background; just give the player an obvious next action within the first second.

items.title: Techniques sheet is a long wall of tiny icons and text
items.what: The MOVES overlay (RIGHT STICK FORWARD / BACK / UP / DOWN sections) is a dense scrollable list of small circle-arrow glyphs + move names + ‘mid · Half point’ labels on a dark brown panel. In the captured frame the lower half of the list is already cut off and every row is the same weight.
items.why: A player who opens MOVES mid-round on a phone needs an at-a-glance answer, not a manual. Uniform tiny rows force reading every line; the most useful full-point attacks do not stand out, so the sheet trains people to close it rather than learn it.
items.how: Re-group by stick direction as collapsible cards, bold the Full-point moves, increase row tap height to ≥44 px, and pin a one-line legend (‘Full point = ippon threat’) at the top. Truncate to the five highest-value moves per direction with a ‘show all’ expand so the first screenful is immediately scannable.

items.title: FIGHT N button and qualifier copy sit on top of the fighters
items.what: On the QUALIFIER vs HasanAbi pre-bout screens the large gold ‘FIGHT 2/3/4’ pill and the flavour bar (‘PATIENT. HE WAITS FOR YOUR WIND-UP…’) are centred directly over the two fighters’ torsos and lead legs, while the ROUND 1/5 chip floats above. The characters are partially covered at the exact moment the player is supposed to study them.
items.why: The first look at the opponent is the moment the player forms a plan. Covering the bodies with UI removes that information and makes the screen feel like a poster instead of a fight about to start.
items.how: Move the flavour bar to the top third (under the round chip) and anchor the FIGHT pill to the lower third, clear of the feet, or turn it into a slim bottom-sheet CTA. Leave the centre 40 % of the canvas as pure fighter silhouette so the matchup is readable before the bout starts.
